title: What is known about 1RB0RE_0LC1LE_0RD1LD_1RA1LF_1LC0RA_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_0LC1LE_0RD1LD_1RA1LF_1LC0RA_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and Collatz-like. The run is a sequence of phases Z → (3Z + c)/2 on a run of zeros; Z mod 4 drives a counter in a short word at the fixed left end. Five phase rules, proved in Lean for any tape left of the counter, cover all but 17 of the first 1,000,000 phases, and those 17 cycle ends are proved one by one. Lean's kernel runs the resulting map 100,000 phases from blank tape (no halt in 1017610 steps); native_decide runs it 1,000,000 phases (10176092 steps). Whether a halting word ever appears depends on the residues of Z at the cycle ends, and those are the 2-adic digits of the orbit: there is no finite law for them. With free residues halting is reachable (a concrete start with a 64,000-bit Z halts), and with fair coin flips the halting rate per cycle-level step is flat, so the heuristic says it halts, far beyond any computation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,606 cells have been visited and 2,752 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweeps of a phase
claims.text: With 4j + 4 zeros left of 1 0 0 0 (100)^n 0 A> at the right end, j sweeps eat 4j zeros and add 2j words 100 to the wall (one sweep: 18n + 64 steps, any tape to the left).

claims.title: The phase map
claims.text: From PS(D, Z) = D 0^Z 1 0 0 E> the next phase start is PS(D', Z') with Z' = (3Z + c)/2, where D' and c depend only on D and Z mod 4: found by running the machine at three Z of the same residue and extrapolating, checked against the plain machine on the 16 phase starts from blank tape (to step 8.7·107).

claims.title: The counter in D
claims.text: For D(a, b) = 0 1 0^a 1 0 1 (001)^b: Z ≡ 1 leaves D alone, Z ≡ 3 makes it D(a−1, b+1), Z stays odd; at a = 0 a phase with Z ≡ 3 resets D to 0 1 0^(3b+5) 1, which continues as D(3b+4, 0) if Z ≡ 3 mod 8 and leaves the family otherwise. Checked for a, b < 16. Now proved for all a, b (see the next claims); the check for a, b < 16 was the first evidence.

claims.title: No halt in 1,500 phases
claims.text: Iterating the phase map from the first phase start (assuming the linear extrapolation, checked as above): resets of the counter at phases 5, 29, 92, 332 stay in the family (cycles of length 11, 35, 107, 323); at phase 1001 (Z has 178 digits) the word leaves it and a second-level counter starts. No halt up to phase 1,500.

claims.title: Whole phases of the level-1 words
claims.text: For D(a, b) = 0 1 0^a 1 0 1 (001)^b and R(a) = 0 1 0^a 1, for every a, b, j: Z = 4j + 9 keeps D(a, b) with Z' = 6j + 15; Z = 4j + 11 turns D(a+1, b) into D(a, b+1) with Z' = 6j + 15, and D(0, b) into R(3b + 5) with Z' = 6j + 18; Z = 4j + 10 turns R(a+1) into D(a, 0) with Z' = 6j + 15. Each phase is the generated start and end rules chained with the sweeps.

claims.title: The first 1001 phases, and no halt in the first 10<sup>177</sup> steps
claims.text: From blank tape the machine reaches PS(D(2, 0), 15) in 457 steps. The level-1 phase map, proved sound, is evaluated by Lean's kernel with exact integers for 1001 phases: the counter resets at phases 5, 29, 92 and 332 stay in the family, and phase 1001 starts at R(971) with Z ≡ 0 mod 4 (178 digits), where the family ends. So the machine runs at least 10<sup>177</sup> steps without halting.

claims.title: The counters, for any word on the left
claims.text: For every tape L left of the counter and every a, b, Z: Z ≡ 1 mod 4 leaves any word ending 0 1 unchanged; Z ≡ 3 turns L 1 0^(a+1) 1 0 1 (001)^b into L 1 0^a 1 0 1 (001)^(b+1) and L 1 0^(a+5) 1 000 1 (001)^b into L 1 0^(a+1) 1 000 1 (001)^(b+2); Z ≡ 2 turns L 1 0^(a+1) 1 into L 1 0^a 1 0 1; Z ≡ 0 turns L 1 0^(a+8) 1 into L 1 0^(a+4) 1 000 1 00 1. Only a counter that has run down reads further left.

claims.title: The 9 kinds of cycle end in the first 10<sup>6</sup> phases
claims.text: 17 of the first 1,000,000 phases are cycle ends, where the counter has run down. They are of 9 kinds, each proved for every b and Z with its short concrete prefix.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>17610</sup> steps
claims.text: The phase map built from these rules, proved sound, is run by Lean's kernel for 100,000 phases from blank tape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>176092</sup> steps
claims.text: The same map, evaluated by compiled code (native_decide), for 1,000,000 phases. Its final state agrees with the exact engine py/phaseiter.py (Z mod 1030, a and b). The real step count is about 10352184; the theorem only claims at least the final Z.

claims.title: No halt in 1,000,000 phases (about 10<sup>352,184</sup> steps), exact
claims.text: py/phaseiter.py runs the machine phase by phase from blank tape with exact integers: each phase's start and sweeps are the Lean rules (jumped over with their exact step count), and the end of each phase is run on the run-length coded tape with the shift rules of symtm.py, the moves that lean/ends.py turns into Lean proofs. No extrapolation. After 1,000,000 phases (4.1 hours) Z has 176,093 digits. Checked against the plain machine on the 17 phase starts to step 8.7·107 and, at each of the first 4,000 phases, on the phase's word with a small Z of the same residue mod 8.

claims.title: The cycles of the counter
claims.text: The counter's cycles end at phases 6, 30, 93, 333 (R(11), R(35), R(107), R(323)), 1002 (R(971): a second-level counter moving by 4), 1511, 2234, 6567 (back to a bare R(6569)), 19692, 59119, 88536, 132982, 199715 and 598126; each cycle is about three times as long as the one before. Short prefixes appear in front of the counter and are eaten again, so the levels do not simply nest.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.41·10<sup>28,643</sup> steps (accelerated run, Quick_Sim)
claims.text: Shawn Ligocki's Quick_Sim.py (github.com/sligocki/busy-beaver, commit cc35611) with recursive rules (-r: a macro machine with a block size it picks itself and a back symbol, rules proved symbolically from repeated tape shapes, and rules whose proofs use earlier rules) runs 2,516,000 loops from blank tape without a halt, in 121 seconds of a 2-minute screen. That is more than 1.41·1028,643 machine steps. It is an outside program, run here without changes; it reported no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Halting words exist
claims.text: With the residue Z mod 4 chosen freely at every phase, 23,305 words of at most 24 cells are reachable from the first phase start, and 7,145 of the (word, residue) pairs met halt, for example 0 1 0 0 1 1 1 0 1 with Z ≡ 3. So halting is not excluded by the words alone; it depends on the residues along the real orbit.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state B reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 4 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (48 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 28 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.50×10<sup>139210</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran the mirrored table (so that the counter is at the left end), with blocks of 3 cells, from blank tape for 3600 seconds and reached step 3.50×10139210 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 5 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: 2,930 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 29,339 of the run (A = 11, U = 0, m = 171, B = 101 0101): 2,930 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 865 bits (about 10520 steps of the machine). 1,410 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 1,428 cells.

claims.title: Some remainder classes halt
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 7,830 found, to depth 17. 169 classes halt. The nearest one is reached by the remainders 3 2 3 2 32 (6 rounds, moduli as above), ending at B = 10 13 0101.

claims.title: No finite law for the cycle ends
claims.text: Each phase is Z' = (3Z + c)/2, so Z<sub>t</sub> mod 8 is fixed by Z<sub>0</sub> mod 2<sup>t+3</sup>, and adding 2<sup>t+2</sup> to Z<sub>0</sub> flips Z<sub>t</sub> mod 8 by 4 without changing an earlier phase. Every sequence of residues at the phases is met by exactly one 2-adic Z<sub>0</sub>: the residues at the cycle ends are the digits of a 3/2-map orbit, as in Mahler's 3/2 problem, not a finite pattern.

claims.title: A halting path in 17 cycle-level steps
claims.text: With Z = 4j + 8 + r, j = 2m + bit and m symbolic (each phase then holds for every Z of that residue mod 8) and the counter run-downs jumped by the Lean rules, a breadth-first search from the first phase start halts after 17 cycle-level steps: the prefix of D walks down 2 1, 1 1 2, 0 1 2 2, 0 0 1, 0 0 0 1 and the next phase halts.

claims.title: A start with a 64,000-bit Z that halts
claims.text: Following a random halting walk of 35 steps and fixing the bits of Z<sub>0</sub> one at a time with the exact engine, a Z<sub>0</sub> of about 64,000 bits makes the exact run from the phase start PS(D(2,0), Z<sub>0</sub>) halt at phase 63,939. The words and phase rules do not exclude halting; only the bits of the blank-tape orbit can.

claims.title: A flat halting rate
claims.text: With fair coin flips for the free bits, 400 walks to depth 2,000 cycle-level steps: 213 halt, at a rate of about 3.7·10<sup>-4</sup> per step that stays flat from the first 250 steps to the last (3.2 to 4.4). The prefix of D outside the counters stays at 1 to 10 gaps: the words recur, they do not grow. If the blank-tape bits behave like coin flips the machine halts with probability 1, but the real orbit makes only about two such steps per threefold cycle (19 in 20,000 phases), so the expected halt lies at a number of phases with hundreds of digits.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It reduces to the orbit of the map Z → (3Z + c)/2 and the nested counters it drives in D. There is no finite law for the residues at the cycle ends, halting paths exist when the residues are free, and a concrete large start halts; whether the blank-tape orbit's residues ever take such a path is a 3/2-map question like Mahler's.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine runs a cousin of the Collatz map. Each phase it turns a run of Z zeros into a wall of 100 words and back into about 3Z/2 zeros. The remainder of Z mod 4 ticks a counter kept in a short word at the far end of the tape, and the counter runs through cycles that grow threefold.

facts.text: No halt in 1,000,000 exact phases from blank tape.
No halt, proved in Lean (kernel): 100,000 phases.
Proved for any word on the left; they cover all but 17 of a million phases.
Each cycle of the counter is about three times longer than the last.
The shortest halting path when the residues at the cycle ends are free.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state B reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 4 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 28 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 29,339 of the run (A = 11, U = 0, m = 171, B = 101 0101): 2,930 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 865 bits (about 10520 steps of the machine). 1,410 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 1,428 cells.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 7,830 found, to depth 17. 169 classes halt. The nearest one is reached by the remainders 3 2 3 2 32 (6 rounds, moduli as above), ending at B = 10 13 0101.

So, granted the class map, the machine halts from blank tape exactly if the orbit ever reaches one of the halting classes. That is a question of the Collatz kind about one orbit of an affine map with remainders, and nothing known decides it: the machine is a cryptid. The orbit computed so far has not reached one.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.525).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,606 cells (10 left of the start, 26,759 right), with a density of 1s of 0.08.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A phase: zeros to wall and back
html: A phase starts with the tape D 0^Z 1 0 0: a short word D at the fixed left end, a run of Z zeros, and the head in state E at the right end. Each sweep the head runs left across a growing wall of 100 words, eats four zeros at the edge of the run, and comes back with two more words on the wall. After about Z/4 sweeps the zeros are used up. The head then works on D, and the wall, now about 3Z/2 cells long, becomes the next run of zeros.
So Z' = (3Z + c)/2, with a small c that depends on D and on Z mod 4. A phase costs about 9Z2/8 steps.

sections.heading: A counter in the word D
html: Write D(a, b) = 0 1 0^a 1 0 1 (001)^b. A phase with Z ≡ 1 mod 4 leaves D alone. A phase with Z ≡ 3 moves one unit from a to b. Z stays odd throughout. When a reaches 0, the next phase with Z ≡ 3 resets the word to 0 1 0^(3b+5) 1, and a new cycle three times as long begins: 11, 35, 107, 323, 971 units.

That holds only if Z ≡ 3 mod 8 at the reset. Otherwise the word grows a second level, a counter that moves by four and two units per phase. From blank tape the first four resets went the simple way. The fifth, at phase 1001, did not.

sections.heading: A million phases, exactly
html: The counter rules for D(a, b) and R(a) are now Lean theorems: each phase is the start of the phase, the sweeps and one of nine end rules, all proved for every size. Lean's kernel then runs the map itself for the first 1001 phases from blank tape, with exact integers, which proves that the machine runs at least 10177 steps without halting.

Past phase 1001 the word grows prefixes, so a new program runs the phases exactly. It jumps over the sweeps with the proved formula and simulates the end of each phase on a compressed tape. Nothing is extrapolated. In 4.1 hours it ran 1,000,000 phases, about 10352,184 steps, without a halt.

Why it stays simple. Five phase rules hold whatever lies further left on the tape: a phase with Z ≡ 1 mod 4 changes nothing, two kinds of counter tick down, and two kinds of restart. Only a counter that has run to zero reads the short word in front of it. That happened just 17 times in the first million phases, in 9 different ways, and each of those 9 is proved too. Chained together, Lean's kernel runs the first 100,000 phases (no halt in 1017,610 steps). Compiled Lean code runs all 1,000,000.

sections.heading: An open, Mahler-like question
html: Each cycle end is decided by the short prefix of D and by Z mod 8. Because Z' = (3Z + c)/2, the residue at phase t is fixed by the last t + 3 binary digits of the starting Z, and each new phase reads one more digit. Every pattern of residues belongs to exactly one 2-adic start, so the question of which residues the real orbit meets is a question about the digits of a 3/2-map orbit, like Mahler's 3/2 problem. No finite law is to be expected.

The words do not protect the machine. Choosing the residues freely, the prefix of D can walk down 2 1, 1 1 2, 0 1 2 2, 0 0 1, 0 0 0 1 and the next phase halts, 17 cycle-level steps from the start. Fixing the bits one by one gives a concrete start, a run of about 64,000 binary digits of zeros, that halts at phase 63,939.

With fair coin flips for the free digits, random walks halt at a steady rate of about one in 2,700 cycle-level steps, and the prefix of D stays short however long the walk. The real orbit makes about two such steps per threefold cycle, so the heuristic says it does halt, but at a number of phases with hundreds of digits. Proving it either way is a 3/2-map problem.

summary: A run of Z zeros is turned into a wall of 100 words and back each phase, Z -> about 3Z/2; Z mod 4 drives a counter in a short word at the fixed end. Five phase rules, proved in Lean for any word to the left, cover all but 17 of the first 10^6 phases, and those are proved one by one: no halt in 10^17610 steps (kernel) or 10^176092 (native_decide). There is no finite law for Z mod 8 at the cycle ends (they are the 2-adic digits of the orbit); with free residues halting is reachable.
